assessments.explanation: The court dismisses the application and remits the matter for re-determination.
The paragraph states that the applicant alleges certain facts.
The applicant claims to be a Chinese citizen fearing persecution for religious reasons.
The applicant describes his dissatisfaction with China's education system and his emotional state.
The applicant details his actions and reactions following a letter he wrote criticizing the education system.
The applicant recounts attending a religious gathering and joining an underground church.
The applicant describes fleeing after police warnings and being accused of illegal religious activities.
The applicant states he fled China and arrived in Canada seeking refugee protection.
The Board decided the applicant was not a refugee due to inability to establish identity.
The Board explained its reasoning for rejecting the applicant's identity documents and credibility.
The paragraph discusses the jurisprudence on the standard of review for legal questions.
The paragraph reviews jurisprudence on the standard of reasonableness for identity findings.
The court states that the standard of review for identity findings is reasonableness.
The paragraph emphasizes the importance of establishing identity and the burden on the claimant.
The jurisprudence indicates that if identity isn't established, further analysis isn't necessary.
The court finds the Board's conclusion on the RIC credible within a range of acceptable outcomes.
The court notes the applicant provided other documents corroborating his identity, which the Board dismissed.
The court observes the Board did not properly assess the authenticity of the additional documents.
The court states that dismissing all identity evidence without examining it was unreasonable.
The court allows the application and remits the case for re-determination.
